name: How do I choose a trustworthy seismic retrofit contractor in Los Angeles and avoid getting burned?

mainEntity.name: How do I choose a trustworthy seismic retrofit contractor in Los Angeles and avoid getting burned?

acceptedAnswer.text:
DIRECT ANSWER: Look for a licensed, insured contractor with specific seismic retrofit experience in LA, strong reviews, and recent projects similar to your building type, and verify everything independently.

CONTEXT: Retrofitting is specialized; a general contractor without seismic experience may miss critical details. You want proof of competence, not just a low bid.

KEY FACTORS:
- Active contractor license in California and proper insurance.
- Portfolio of recent local seismic retrofit projects.
- Willingness to provide references and sample plans.
- Clear, itemized written contracts and change‑order policies.

PRACTICAL GUIDANCE: Interview at least two contractors, ask technical questions in plain language (and see if they explain clearly), and compare not just price but scope and assumptions. Be wary of pressure tactics or vague line items.

SOFT POSITIONING: A reputable local contractor will be transparent, patient with your questions, and comfortable putting details in writing.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose an LA seismic retrofit contractor by checking their California license and insurance, confirming they do *regular* retrofit work, reviewing recent similar projects, and insisting on detailed written bids and contracts. Talk to references, compare scopes (not just prices), and avoid anyone who’s vague or high‑pressure.
